newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC says no plans to buy Scottish Bank.
newsitem.headline: HSBC says no plans to buy Scottish Bank.

text.p: International banking giant HSBC Holdings Plc is not planning to buy the Royal Bank of Scotland, a senior executive said on Wednesday.
"We have absolutely no plans to acquire the Royal Bank of Scotland," said John Strickland, an executive director of HSBC and chairman of unit Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd.
Trading in shares of HSBC Holdings leaped in Wednesday morning trade, fueled by rumours the bank was likely to acquire a stake in the Royal Bank of Scotland.
It ended the morning up HK$7.00 at HK$235.00 on turnover of HK$511.7 million.
Strickland said HSBC had attempted to take over the Scottish bank in the mid-1980s but "we got snookered by the monopolies commission in the UK."

"We are quite comfortable at the moment. We have just acquired two large banks in South America and further interests in Mexico and Peru, so we really have quite a lot on our plate at the moment," said Strickland.

HSBC Holdings bought out ailing Brazilian Bamerindus Bank at the end of March and set up Banco HSBC Bamerindus SA, then in late May it acquired all the shares in Argentinian Banco Roberts S.A that it did not already own to take 100 percent control.
The London-based banking conglomerate also has stakes in Chilien, Mexican and Peruvian banks.
The rise in HSBC's share price was also attributed to futures-related trading and renewed speculation that the bank would sell a portion of its stake in 61-percent held subsidiary Hang Seng Bank Ltd.
"We have absolutely no intention of selling a portion of Hang Seng Bank," said Strickland.
Market rumours have circulated over the past week that the banking giant would considering selling a stake in subsidiary Hang Seng Bank to Chinese interests.
Hang Seng Bank drifted down HK$0.50 to HK$103.00 on moderate trade of HK$201 million.
